# Research Question

How do people in pre-industrial societies learn to make tools?

## Sub-questions
1. Do hunter-gatherers have a unique learning pattern compared with groups practicing other types of subsistence strategies?

2. Do learning strategies change across different developmental periods? (More specific hypothesis: will the frequency of social learning decrease through time?)

3. What are some major transmission biases involved? (kin-based? context(success)-based?)

# Motivation/Significance

1. At the most basic level, this study provides the most in-depth descriptive investigation on this topic so far.

2. It can help improving the external validity of archaeological experimental design.

3. It can serve as a middle-range framework to better understand the formation of archaeological records.

# Data sources and searching strategies
0. Scope of study: Global sample

1. EHRAF World Cultures:  subject "transmission of skills" + key word "tools". This combination yields 133 paragraphs in 96 documents across 72 cultures. (thank you to Carol! Also remember to try specific name of tools like spear/knife/etc. Another keywords include make/made/makes/making.)

2. EHRAF World Cultures: key word "practice" + "tool"? (haven't tried it)

3. Other ethnoarchaeological works I have read before

# Variables

1. Area: using eHRAF's classification system

2. Society: using eHRAF's classification system

3. Code: using eHRAF's classification system

4. Subsistence: hunter-gatherer, primarily hunter-gatherer, horticulturalist, agro-pastarolist, intensive agriculturalist, commercial economy, other subsistence combinations (eHRAF's classification system)

5. Year of observation: eHRAF?

6. Location: following the author's description

7. Location(type): indoor, settlement, field

8. Age of learner: precise age if it is explicitly described

9. Age group of learner: Infancy, Early Adulthood, Middle Childhood, Adolescence, Adult

10. Number of learner: precise number or number group?

11. Age of model: precise age if it is explicitly described

12. Age group of model: Infancy, Early Adulthood, Middle Childhood, Adolescence, Adult (<50), Adult (>50)

13. Number of model: precise number or number group?

14. Transmission modes: horizontal/vertical/oblique

15. Social relationship: mother/father/etc.

16. Transmission bias: using Kendal's (2018) framework

17. Learning procesess: following Garfield et al. (2016), imitation/emulation, local enhancement, stimulus enhancement, collective learning, collective learning play, collective learning role play, teaching, teaching demonstration, teaching storytelling, individual learning

18. Perceived difficulty: difficult/moderate/easy

19. Time spent:

20. Technology: ?

21. Raw material: stone, clay, plant, bones

22. Access to raw materials: difficult/moderate/easy

23. Restriction of status involved: gender? wealth? religious status?

24. Note (habit, context) 

25. Reference
